time_basis: Selected records retain original SCLK, LMST and LTST. UTC range comes from PDS4 labels; no interpolated per-row UTC is asserted.

sampling.operation: Nearest original observation; no averaging, gap filling, spatial interpolation or forecast. Later drive excluded; only sol16 00:00–13:45 LMST included.

location.basis: Stationary MEDA ancillary interval, anchored by exact Yeehgo image SCLK to its PDS PLACES site 3 / drive 386 observation station.
location.registration: Approximate observation station. Residual PLACES-to-DEM registration error is not quantified; no local coverage radius inferred.

variables.ats1_kelvin: MEDA calibrated ATS1 local air temperature near the mast unit at 50 degrees; not a merged free-air temperature.

quality: Source archives plus format/unit/time checks. These chosen products supply no per-row quality flags. Missing/sentinel values remain unavailable.
limitations: Historical reference point, not current weather, route-wide measurements or a forecast.
No spatial weather gradient inferred from one stationary observation location.
No wind or humidity: archive cautions exclude pre-sol36 wind and pre-sol63 humidity from science use.
No ionizing radiation or radiation dose layer; MEDA optical radiation is not ionizing dose.
Pressure uncertainty is empty here and its XML unit says kelvin; no uncertainty value/unit is inferred.
ATS1 measures local air near one instrument; rover thermal influence and independent scientific validation remain unresolved.

columns.name: SOLAR_LONGITUDE_ANGLE
columns.description: Solar azimuth angle relative to M2020 local level frame rotated 180 degrees over the X axis (+X points to the local north direction; +Z points up; +Y completes the right handed frame, pointing to the local west direction; the origin is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover) It is the angle between the positive X-axis and the orthogonal projection of the Sun onto the XY plane. It increases in the counterclockwise sense about the positive Z-axis. Range of -180 to 180 degrees

columns.name: SOLAR_ZENITHAL_ANGLE
columns.description: Solar elevation angle relative to M2020 local level frame rotated 180 degrees over the X axis (+X points to the local north direction; +Z points up; +Y completes the right handed frame, pointing to the local west direction; the origin is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover) It is the angle between the direction of the Sun and the positive Z-axis. A value of 0 degrees represents Sun at frame zenith, while a value of 180 degrees represents Sun at frame nadir. Range of 0 to 180 degrees.

columns.name: ROVER_POSITION_X
columns.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the X-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

columns.name: ROVER_POSITION_Y
columns.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the y-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

columns.name: ROVER_POSITION_Z
columns.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the z-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

columns.name: ROVER_VELOCITY
columns.description: Rover velocity

columns.name: ROVER_PITCH
columns.description: Rover pitch, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +Y-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

columns.name: ROVER_YAW
columns.description: Rover yaw, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +Z-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

columns.name: ROVER_ROLL
columns.description: Rover roll, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +X-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

columns.name: MASTHEAD_AZIMUTH
columns.description: Masthead azimuth angle. Range of -180 to 180 degrees. An azimuth angle of 1 degree represents rover looking backward, an azimuth angle of 91 degrees represents rover looking to the left, an azimuth angle of -179 degrees represents rover looking forward, and an azimuth angle of -89 degrees represents rover looking to the right

columns.name: MASTHEAD_ELEVATION
columns.description: Masthead elevation angle. Range of 0 to 360 degrees. An elevation angle of 1 degree represents rover looking down, an elevation angle of 91 degrees represents rover looking forward and an elevation angle of 181 degrees represents rover looking at the zenith
